title: Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon
description: Robert Burns's song of the banks of the Doon, both verses: Burns's words as James Johnson printed them (1792), to the tune as G. F. Graham printed it (1848). For 2 to 4 singers: the soprano sings the melody, the alto sings close beneath it, the tenor fills in the chord and the bass sings the bass line. Slow and tender, in a gentle 6/8.

credits.tune: "The Caledonian Hunt's Delight", by James Miller, fashioned into a tune by Stephen Clarke (printed 1792; sung here as G. F. Graham printed it in 1848)

licence.words: public domain: Robert Burns died 1796; printed 1792
licence.tune: public domain: printed 1792 in the Scots Musical Museum, whose index credits "the Music by Mr James Millar Writer in Edinr." (his death year not found; already a writer, that is a Scots law agent, in Edinburgh in 1792, and called "Mr James Miller, Depute teind-clerk, Edinburgh" by William Stenhouse, who knew him, so long dead before 1956); Burns, in a letter to George Thomson of November 1794 quoted by William Stenhouse (died 1827) and by G. F. Graham, says Stephen Clarke (died 1797) fashioned Miller's air into the tune; the Museum's editor and publisher James Johnson died 1811; the tune sung here as printed in 1848 by G. F. Graham (1789-1867, dates from the University of Toronto Library's catalogue record for The Songs of Scotland, on archive.org)
licence.arrangement: original, written for Stackapella: the Museum's unsigned bass read only to check the chords, and J. T. Surenne's piano part in Graham not used (his death year not found in a seen source); the alto, tenor and bass are new, one note a syllable. Accepted exceptions (singable.py): the tune's own rhythm as Graham prints it: its one- and two-semiquaver pickups ("How", "How", "And", "Thou'll", "That", "Thou", "De-" and "Oft"; in verse 2 "To", "And", "And", "Wi'", "Fu'", "And" and "But,") and the short last notes of its lines (the semiquaver G ending "Doon,", the quaver on "fair;") leave a quaver's rest before each line, half a second at 40 to the dotted crotchet but a third of a beat, under rule 1's half beat; a longer rest would cut the turn or make a pickup shorter than 0.15 seconds, so rule 2 counts each verse as one breath though the tune rests half a second every 6 seconds; the alto, tenor and bass rest a dotted quaver before each line and pass.
licence.source: Burns's words as Johnson printed them (1792), to the tune as G. F. Graham printed it (1848). The words: The Scots Musical Museum, vol. 4, published by James Johnson (Edinburgh: Johnson & Co., 1792), no. 374, "The Banks o' Doon", p. 387, marked "Slow & tender", printed in G in 6/8; both stanzas as printed ("bonie", "luve", "fause luver staw" kept); the index entry "Ye Banks and braes o' bonie Don - Burns, the Music by Mr James Millar Writer in Edinr." on the index's page VI; read from the 1792 copy in the National Library of Scotland, archive.org/details/scotsmusicalmuse04rugg, page images n88 (the song) and n11 (the index), and seen too in the reissue printed from the same plates, The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 4 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons, 1839), archive.org/details/scotishmusicalmu04john, page image n90, whose index reads "James Millar, Writer in Edinr.". The tune: G. F. Graham, The Songs of Scotland, vol. 2 (Edinburgh: Wood & Co., 1848; some copies dated 1849), "Ye Banks and Braes o' Bonnie Doon", arranged by J. T. Surenne, pp. 4 and 5, University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library copy, archive.org/details/songsofscotlanda00grah, page images n189 and n190 (a later undated issue; the National Library of Scotland's copies of vol. 2, from the same plates, are dated 1848, Glen 214.a, archive.org/details/songsofscotland01grah, image n4, and 1849, Ing.128, on the title page), in G in 6/8 and written here in G, a dotted crotchet to the beat: Johnson's notes in Graham's smoother rhythm (even quavers where Johnson has Scotch snaps or dotted pairs, the snaps on "bloom", "weary" and "never" kept, a dotted turn on "braes", "chant" and the "o'" of "minds me o'", and one quaver for "Thou'll"); Graham's grace note and pause on "thorn" and his altered words ("Ye'll", "ye warbling birds", "wanton through", "flow'ry", "love", "lover stole") left out. Breaths written in for beginners: before each new line the line's last note gives up time, a quaver from "fair" and "thorn" (verse 2: "twine", "tree"), whose two-semiquaver pickups ("How", "Thou"; verse 2: "And", "And") stay in time, and a semiquaver from "Doon", "birds", "care", "bird" and "joys" (verse 2: "Doon", "luve", "mine", "rose", "rose"), with the next line's one-quaver pickup ("How", "And", "Thou'll", "That", "De-"; verse 2: "To", "And", "Wi'", "Fu'", "But,") starting a semiquaver late; verse 1's last "turn" sung as a quaver and verse 2's "Oft" starting a semiquaver late; the alto, tenor and bass rest a dotted quaver before each line and come in a semiquaver late.
